findings.title: index.json by_severity shows COSMETIC: 1 while open_findings is 0, making field semantics ambiguous
findings.detail: The by_severity field in .audits/index.json showed {CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 0, COSMETIC: 1} while open_findings was 0. The field appears to have been tracking the previous run's fixed-finding count by severity rather than currently-open findings, but its position next to open_findings and its name imply it counts open findings by severity. Any tool consuming this field (e.g., the Proposer scoring algorithm, audit-status.sh, or the online-eval aggregator) would infer 1 open COSMETIC finding exists when none do, potentially inflating scoring or producing incorrect status banners.
findings.fix_sketch: Reset by_severity to {CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 0, COSMETIC: 0} so it correctly reflects zero open findings. Alternatively, rename to fixed_this_run_by_severity to remove ambiguity.
findings.fix_summary: Reset by_severity to {CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 0, COSMETIC: 0} in index.json to correctly reflect zero open findings. Also updated last_updated and fixed_this_run count.

findings.title: closing_pr: null in 20260802T080000Z.json violates schema — should be integer 0 for local-only fixes
findings.detail: The self-heal-pipeline.md spec is explicit: 'If the closure landed without a PR (rare; only for local-only repos), use 0 and explain in fix_summary.' The 20260802T080000Z.json scan file used null for closing_pr instead of the integer 0. The regression-detector verdict format REGRESSION:<original_id>:<closing_pr> requires an integer value; null would cause string-split parsing to produce 'null' as the third segment, breaking downstream regression tracking. Additionally the finding was missing its fix_summary field.
findings.fix_sketch: Change closing_pr from null to 0 and add fix_summary per the closed.json contract.
findings.fix_summary: Changed closing_pr from null to 0 and added fix_summary to 20260802T080000Z.json to conform to the schema defined in self-heal-pipeline.md.

findings.title: audit_id in 20260730T041253Z.json uses 'nightly-YYYY-MM-DD' format instead of 'audit-<compacted-timestamp>'
findings.detail: The plan.md schema specifies the audit_id format as 'audit-<compacted-timestamp>' (e.g., 'audit-20260520T2300Z'). The 20260730T041253Z.json file uses 'nightly-2026-07-30', which is a different format. All other recent scan files use the correct 'audit-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ' format. While non-breaking today, inconsistent audit_id formats would break any future tooling that parses audit_id to extract timestamps or identify scan provenance.
findings.fix_sketch: Change audit_id from 'nightly-2026-07-30' to 'audit-20260730T041253Z' to match the file's own timestamp and the schema convention.
findings.fix_summary: Updated audit_id in 20260730T041253Z.json from 'nightly-2026-07-30' to 'audit-20260730T041253Z' to conform to the schema.
